hlni.insight: Business Organization & Management appears in Semester I of both the JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management 2025-26 programmes.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles inherently partition subjects like management and accounting.
hlni.viewerChange: Student stops using degree titles as a shortcut for curriculum content and starts comparing specific module lists.
hlni.payoff: The student moves B.Com back to their active research list, demonstrating that verifying modules is a better selection method than binary assumptions.

candidate.reelTitle: Beyond the Title: B.Com vs BBA
candidate.creativeAngle: Using verified syllabus overlap to challenge title-based assumptions
candidate.objective: Help students move from binary degree exclusion to evidence-based investigation
candidate.targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: Student discarding B.Com file
shots.visual: A student holds a folder labeled B.Com and drops it into a 'Discard' bin, keeping a BBA folder.
shots.dialogue: I thought B.Com was only for accounting, so I crossed it off my list.
shots.cameraPerformance: Close-up on the student's face, showing decisive but dismissive body language.

shots.name: Student looking confused at lists
shots.visual: Student opens two official PDFs on a laptop side-by-side. The B.Com and BBA documents are visible.
shots.dialogue: But then I checked the actual Semester One syllabi.
shots.cameraPerformance: Camera pans from the student's skeptical expression to the laptop screen.

shots.name: Close up of shared subject
shots.visual: Graphic overlay zooms into a row in both PDFs showing 'Business Organization & Management'.
shots.dialogue: Wait. Both programmes list Business Organization and Management?
shots.cameraPerformance: Dramatic zoom-in on the shared text; student leans in, eyes wide.

shots.name: Comparing source documents
shots.visual: Student points to the page numbers in both documents: JOY B.Com 2025-26, p.5 and BBA 2025-26, p.9.
shots.dialogue: Both JOY University degrees include this management module in Semester One.
shots.cameraPerformance: Over-the-shoulder shot showing the student comparing the two official documents.

shots.name: Student re-evaluating shortlist
shots.visual: Student retrieves the B.Com folder from the bin and moves it to the 'Investigate' pile.
shots.dialogue: If titles don't tell the whole story, I need to check the full module depth.
shots.cameraPerformance: Calm, deliberate movement; student looks focused and analytical.

shots.name: Student opening a fresh notebook
shots.visual: Student starts writing a list of course modules to compare.
shots.dialogue: Compare the syllabus, not just the title.
shots.cameraPerformance: Medium shot of student writing; the screen fades to black.

productionNotes.camera: Handheld for authenticity, sharp focus on documents
productionNotes.casting: Student in +2 uniform or casual college attire

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Challenge the assumption that B.Com lacks management by showing official syllabus overlap, prompting a shift from binary exclusion to detailed investigation.

storySpine.startingBelief: B.Com is only about accounting and lacks management subjects.
storySpine.studentSituation: Student is preparing a shortlist for higher education and has excluded B.Com based on this belief.
storySpine.observation: Student notices 'Business Organization & Management' listed in the Semester I syllabus for both JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management.
storySpine.focus: The specific overlap of a management course in a B.Com programme.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: If the course titles are shared, the assumption that B.Com is exclusively accounting is factually incomplete.
storySpine.changedAction: Student adds B.Com back to their provisional shortlist to conduct further course-specific research.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: Student moves B.Com from an 'exclude' folder to a 'check syllabus details' folder.
storySpine.channelExperience: Viewer sees the student physically re-organizing their degree shortlist after cross-referencing the official university documents.

selected.title: Beyond the Title: B.Com vs BBA
selected.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles dictate the entire content of the course.
selected.hlni: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents whose covers say students admitted from 2025–26 onwards.
selected.viewerChange: From binary exclusion to provisional investigation of actual programme modules.
selected.concept: Using verified syllabus overlap to challenge title-based assumptions.
selected.support: Official JOY University PDF, B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9; covers identify the 2025–26-onwards cohort.
methodSteps: Identify the specific programme and document cohort.
Show the inspected course-title row in each source.
Use this bounded overlap to investigate the full course, rather than assume degree titles partition subjects.
selected.interpretationRule: The supplied rows establish this shared title in these two documents only; they do not establish identical teaching, depth, assessment or availability.
selected.visibleProof: Two real cited rows correct a title-based assumption while retaining programme/version scope.
selected.payoff: A more nuanced, evidence-based approach to programme selection.
selected.limitations: No universal overlap, identical content, exclusivity, current-admissions or career inference. BBA later sections are inconsistent; use only the inspected row.

demonstration.input: B.Com Accounting & Finance (JOY University 2025-26) vs BBA Entrepreneurship Management (JOY University 2025-26)
demonstration.observation: The same core management module appears in both programmes.
demonstration.nextQuestion: Does this degree offer the management depth I need, regardless of the B.Com label?
